profile.diet: Adults eat mostly mid-water prey: mullets, pinfish, marine catfishes; crabs are a spring favorite at inlets
profile.depth: Normal habitat to about 30 m; tolerates salinities from fresh to about 47 ppt
profile.behavior: Migratory and heat-loving. Adults arrive in the Florida Keys in April once surface water reaches about 26 C, peak in May (26-28 C) and leave in June (27-29 C). Cold fronts push them to warmer, deeper water, and juveniles leave creeks below about 20 C.
profile.spawning: April to June in the Florida Keys
profile.regulations_note: Florida prohibits the commercial sale of tarpon. Check FWC rules before keeping any tarpon.

factors.value_notes: Keys tagging (FWC and FIU): most adults arrived in April once water reached 26 C and left in June at 27-29 C, with peak presence in May (26-28 C). Satellite tagging follows a 26 C isotherm. Guides cite 75-80 F (24-27 C), biting best in the low 80s F. Juvenile tarpon left creeks below 20 C, and adults retreat to warmer, deeper water in cold snaps, so cooler water is a hard stop.
factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside the {ideal_min}-{ideal_max} C range where tarpon run.

factors.value_notes: In the Keys, adults are present mainly April to June (spawning season), with lowest numbers August to October. The run is applied to Miami-area inlets as a judgment call; Miami's timing may differ a little.

value_text.peak: It is peak tarpon season (May and June), when adults are in South Florida passes.
value_text.in_season: It is tarpon run season (about April to July).
value_text.off: It is outside the spring and early-summer tarpon run, so far fewer tarpon are in South Florida passes.

factors.value_notes: Angler guidance only: tarpon feed in passes when the tide is moving. The mapping from tide stage to score is a judgment call.

value_text.falling: The tide is falling ({station}); moving water through passes is when tarpon feed.
value_text.rising: The tide is rising ({station}); moving water through passes is when tarpon feed.
value_text.slack_low: The tide is near low ({station}), so little water is moving and tarpon feed less.
value_text.slack_high: The tide is near high ({station}), so little water is moving and tarpon feed less.

factors.value_notes: Tarpon travel through inlets and passes, where crabs and baitfish are carried out on the tide.

value_text.inlet: This is an inlet or pass. Tarpon travel through passes and feed on crabs and baitfish the tide carries.

factors.value_notes: Angler guidance only: tarpon are fished day and night at passes and bridges, with low light and night often rated well. The mapping is a judgment call.

value_text.night: It is night, a favored time for tarpon around passes and bridges.
value_text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time tarpon feed actively.
value_text.dawn: It is dawn, a low-light time tarpon feed actively.
value_text.day: It is daylight, when tarpon fishing is usually slower.

factors.value_notes: Tarpon tolerate 0-47 ppt; not needed for scoring.
Bridges and lit docks are key tarpon spots. Needs a bridge dataset (planned).
